papers.design: Randomized controlled trial; 162 students; three parallel groups
papers.finding: After 20 minutes of 528 Hz-labelled instrumental music, salivary CREB was higher and GRP78 lower than in the no-music group. Stroop performance did not differ. Table 1 gives 528 Hz and control the same BDNF significance label, despite the more positive abstract.

papers.finding: Daily sound meditation incorporating recorded 528 Hz audio and acoustic instruments outperformed remotely delivered music on anxiety, depression, salivary cortisol and blood pressure. papers.summary: Daily sound meditation incorporating recorded 528 Hz audio and acoustic instruments outperformed remotely delivered music on anxiety, depression, salivary cortisol and blood pressure. papers.title: Effect of 528 Hz Music on the Endocrine System and Autonomic Nervous System
papers.authors: Akimoto K, Hu A, Yamaguchi T, Kobayashi H.

papers.limitation: Nine healthy adults took part. These short-term saliva findings need independent replication in larger samples.

papers.title: Study On Impact of Sound Frequency on Human Well Being Using Randomized Block Design
papers.authors: Unhale SI, Khairnar SL, Joshi MA.
papers.kind: Reported randomized block experiment; RCT eligibility unresolved
papers.design: Reported randomized block experiment; RCT eligibility unresolved
papers.finding: The report includes 57 participants aged 17–20 and exposures labelled 379, 430 and 528 Hz. Mean ratings for calmness, focus and stress relief were higher at 430 Hz than at 528 Hz. A pooled before-and-after heart-rate reduction from 80.56 to 79.25 bpm does not separate the frequencies.
papers.summary: The report includes 57 participants aged 17–20 and exposures labelled 379, 430 and 528 Hz. Mean ratings for calmness, focus and stress relief were higher at 430 Hz than at 528 Hz. A pooled before-and-after heart-rate reduction from 80.56 to 79.25 bpm does not separate the frequencies.
papers.limitation: The allocation and repeated-exposure structure are unclear; group sizes, sequence concealment and frequency-specific heart-rate comparisons are not adequately reported. topic.description: A small, active research field with promising findings for short-term stress and anxiety.
paragraphs: Oxytocin almost doubled within five minutes of listening to 528 Hz music in the 2018 study; the increase with 440 Hz music was not statistically significant. Other studies report reductions in anxiety, cortisol and blood pressure.

Several randomized trials now complement the earlier human and laboratory studies. The evidence remains preliminary: samples are generally small, blinding and reporting vary, follow-up is short, and some outcomes show no significant change.

records.originalNote:
“The current results show that in IC50 of ethanol, the frequency of 528 Hz increased cells viability about 20% and the level of ROS production has been reduced up to 100%.”

“In this research the complex effects of two agents such as ethanol along with 528 Hz sound wave was studied and results of human astrocyte cell culture exposed with ethanol and 528 Hz sound wave showed that the ethanol damages reduced by the sound wave and therefore it can be useful for alcohol addicted peoples.”

“The neural changes induced by alcohol consumption may be related to the disorder of signaling pathways such as protein expression and gene transcription at the cellular level. Therefore, the use of these sound waves can be useful to reduce the toxic effects of ethanol on astrocytes cells culture.”

records.title: Study On Impact of Sound Frequency on Human Well Being Using Randomized Block Design
records.authors: Unhale SI, Khairnar SL, Joshi MA.
records.kind: Reported randomized block experiment; RCT eligibility unresolved
records.design: Reported randomized block experiment; RCT eligibility unresolved
records.finding: The report includes 57 participants aged 17–20 and exposures labelled 379, 430 and 528 Hz. Mean ratings for calmness, focus and stress relief were higher at 430 Hz than at 528 Hz. A pooled before-and-after heart-rate reduction from 80.56 to 79.25 bpm does not separate the frequencies.
records.summary: The report includes 57 participants aged 17–20 and exposures labelled 379, 430 and 528 Hz. Mean ratings for calmness, focus and stress relief were higher at 430 Hz than at 528 Hz. A pooled before-and-after heart-rate reduction from 80.56 to 79.25 bpm does not separate the frequencies.
records.limitation: The allocation and repeated-exposure structure are unclear; group sizes, sequence concealment and frequency-specific heart-rate comparisons are not adequately reported. A pooled change cannot identify the effect of 528 Hz. Randomized block design is a randomization method, but the reporting is insufficient to confirm a qualifying controlled trial here.
records.ratingBasis: The methods state random assignment within eight blocks, while also describing three exposures per participant. Retain the author-reported design and mark RCT eligibility unresolved rather than infer an independently verified RCT.

records.kind: Author-reported randomized controlled conference study; 28 adolescents
records.design: Author-reported randomized controlled conference study; 28 adolescents

records.summary: The paper describes randomized groups receiving a sound device, active music therapy or control. It reports improvements in emotional self-ratings, without a significant difference between the two therapy groups.
records.limitation: Only eight participants received the sound device. The described frequencies are 240–500 Hz with a 410–450 Hz base; 528 Hz appears in the conceptual Solfeggio mapping, rather than as a verified delivered tone. This is related frequency-family context with uncertain transfer to 528 Hz listening.
